books.section: The Jazz Age and the Great Depression (1920–1933)

primary_sources: Rollin Kirby, “Classroom in Proposed Bryan University of Tennessee,” 1925

stimulus.source_note: Rollin Kirby, “Classroom in Proposed Bryan University of Tennessee,” 1925, public domain.
stimulus.text: A 1925 cartoon by Rollin Kirby, titled “Classroom in Proposed Bryan University of Tennessee,” shows a teacher bound and gagged, pointing at a wall chart labeled “Map of the Earth” that shows a flat earth with the lands above a “VOID.” A portrait labeled “PREXY” — William Jennings Bryan — hangs on the wall beside a poster of “HELL.”

source: original; stimulus image from the shared pool, Rollin Kirby, “Classroom in Proposed Bryan University of Tennessee,” 1925, public domain.
stem: The cultural conflict shown in the cartoon is most similar to which of the following other conflicts of the 1920s?

options.text: The clash between Prohibition supporters and those who drank, over whether the law should enforce traditional morality.
The debate over the League of Nations, over whether the United States should join international organizations.
options.misconception: The League debate was about foreign policy, not about traditional morality against modern life at home.

options.text: The fight over the Smoot-Hawley Tariff, over whether trade barriers would help American farmers.
options.misconception: The tariff fight was about economics and farm prices, and it came in 1930, after the decade’s cultural fights.

options.text: The dispute over the Teapot Dome scandal, over whether cabinet officials had taken bribes.
options.misconception: Teapot Dome was a corruption scandal, not a clash between traditional and modern ways of living.

figures.caption: Rollin Kirby, “Classroom in Proposed Bryan University of Tennessee,” 1925
figures.alt: A 1925 cartoon shows a teacher bound and gagged pointing at a flat-earth wall map while a portrait of Bryan hangs on the wall

rationales.A: Both fights are the 1920s’ struggle between traditional and modern America: older rural and religious values enforced by law against newer urban ways of living. Background: Prohibition, under the Eighteenth Amendment of 1919, tried to use the law to enforce traditional morality on drinking.
rationales.B: The League debate was about foreign policy. It was not about traditional morality against modern life at home.
rationales.C: The tariff fight was about economics and farm prices. It also came in 1930, after the decade’s cultural fights.
rationales.D: Teapot Dome was a corruption scandal. It was not a clash between traditional and modern ways of living.
rationales.general:
1. Name the cartoon’s fight. Traditional religious values, backed by law, against modern science in the classroom.
2. Name the pattern. The 1920s kept staging the same fight: older values enforced by law against newer ways of living.
3. Test the options. Only Prohibition matches that shape, with the law enforcing traditional morality on drinking.
4. Rule out the rest. The League, the tariff, and Teapot Dome are about foreign policy, economics, and corruption.
Remember: when a decade repeats one fight in many places, look for the same shape, not the same subject.
